concepts.label: Diaspora novel corpus
concepts.definition: The literature project on diaspora novels.

memories.text: Cite literary works in MLA style: author, title in italics, publisher and year, with (Author page) in the text; this applies to course essays only.
The book manuscript uses Chicago notes-bibliography style with footnotes, not MLA.
Write a close reading: quote the passage, name its form and diction, interpret the effect, and link it back to the argument.

fields.trigger: write a close reading of a passage
steps: identify its form, diction and imagery
link the reading back to the chapter's argument

memories.text: State the thesis in the first paragraph as a contestable claim, not a summary of the plot.
Quote primary texts from a named edition with page numbers and keep them apart from secondary criticism.
Manuscripts are held in the university special collections; request items at least 48 hours ahead with the reading room form.
Public-domain texts are on Project Gutenberg and scans on HathiTrust; always record which edition you used.
A mistranslated key word in the English edition undermined a chapter's argument; check central terms in the original.

fields.situation: an argument rests on one word in a translated text
fields.do_instead: check the original language for central terms

memories.text: Paraphrase and cite; never copy more than four words in a row without quotation marks.
Organised the chapter by theme instead of chronology because the novels overlap in time.
Journal essays in literary studies run to 8,000 words including notes.
At the May symposium a respondent asked for closer engagement with postcolonial theory.
Build the text corpus: get permission, record edition and year, clean the OCR errors, and tag each file with metadata.

fields.trigger: add a novel to the corpus
steps: get permission or confirm the licence
